answer: Each round the registry shuffles its seats into a secret chain and releases one sealed opal to the first link; every seat must sign the token and hand it onward within a tight deadline, and only the carrier standing at the summit when the round closes is paid. Clones add links rather than throughput: a thousand extra seats stretch the relay and its timing risk without buying parallelism, and one missed handoff voids the bond of every seat downstream. Idle capacity sits like a tundra, so reward per fake identity collapses as the attacker scales.
